common.siteDescription: Free forex education, tools, and analysis.

home.placeholder: Public surface — scaffold placeholder. See docs/logs/DEVLOG.md for module status.
home.heroBody: Free forex education, tools, and analysis.
home.glossaryLead: Plain-language definitions for the terms you will meet on every chart.
home.newsletterBody: Analysis and education, delivered as it publishes.
home.faqLead: The things new traders ask us most often.
home.faqA1: Yes. Every lesson, glossary entry and market article on this site is free to read.
home.faqQ2: Do I need trading experience to start?
home.faqA2: No. The material starts from first principles and builds up, so a complete beginner can follow it.
home.faqA3: No. Everything here is educational. Nothing on this site is a recommendation to buy or sell any instrument.
home.faqQ4: How often is new analysis published?
home.faqA4: New articles and analysis are published regularly; the latest always appear on this page and in the News section.
home.exploreTitle: Everything a trader needs, in one place
home.exploreLead: Lessons, calculators, live market context and daily analysis — each one useful on its own, and considerably better together.
home.exploreLearnBody: Structured courses that start at first principles and build towards a repeatable trading process.
home.exploreToolsBody: Position size, pip value, margin and profit — worked out before the trade rather than after it.
home.exploreCalendarBody: Every release that moves a pair, with its impact rating and the numbers as they land.
home.exploreNewsBody: What happened, why it mattered and what it changes — written for people who trade, not for headline readers.
home.exploreAnalysisBody: Chart-led breakdowns and trade ideas from the desk, published as the session develops.
home.exploreGlossaryBody: Plain-language definitions for every term you will meet on a chart, cross-linked as you read.
home.exploreMarketsBody: Rates, trading sessions and currency strength, so you know what the market is doing before you open a chart.
home.exploreAboutBody: Who writes this material, how the site is funded, and what we will never do with your attention.
home.videoTitle: Start with the six that matter
home.videoLead: Short lessons that build in order — what the market is, how to read it, and how to size a trade before you place one.
home.videoBasicsTitle: What the forex market actually is
home.videoBasicsBody: Who trades currencies, why a pair has two prices, and what you are really buying when you buy EUR/USD.
home.videoCandlesticksBody: Open, high, low, close — and what a single candle can and cannot tell you about the next one.
home.videoRiskBody: Deciding what a trade may cost you before you take it, and the arithmetic that turns that decision into a lot size.
home.videoLevelsBody: Why price hesitates in the same places twice, how to mark a level honestly, and when a level has stopped mattering.
home.videoPlanBody: Turning a setup you like into written rules — entry, invalidation, target and the days you do not trade at all.
home.videoPsychologyBody: The predictable moments where discipline fails, and the small process changes that make failing harder.
home.highlightsTitle: Built to be understood, not to impress
home.highlightsLead: Six commitments that shape every lesson, article and definition on this site.
home.highlightPlainLanguageBody: Jargon is defined the first time it appears, and linked to the glossary every time after.
home.highlightWorkedExamplesBody: Numbers are shown being calculated, not asserted — so you can reproduce them on your own trade.
home.highlightRiskIncludedTitle: Risk is part of the lesson
home.highlightRiskIncludedBody: Never a footnote. If material shows a way to enter, it shows what happens when the trade is wrong.
home.highlightFreeToReadBody: Every lesson, article and glossary entry is readable without signing up or handing over an email.
home.highlightMultilingualBody: The site is written to be translated, right down to reading direction — not bolted on afterwards.
home.highlightNoHypeBody: We teach a process and publish analysis. We do not sell tips, and nothing here is advice to trade.
home.latestNewsLead: What moved, and why it mattered — written for people who trade.

economicCalendar.title: Economic calendar
economicCalendar.intro: Every scheduled release that moves the majors, grouped by day — with the forecast, the previous print, and the actual figure the moment it lands.
economicCalendar.legendIntro: Impact is how much volatility a release is expected to cause in the listed currency — not whether the number itself is good or bad.
economicCalendar.impactHighBody: Rate decisions, inflation, employment. Expect fast, wide moves in the listed currency.
economicCalendar.impactMediumBody: Secondary data that usually moves price, but rarely sets the day's direction on its own.
economicCalendar.impactLowBody: Minor releases. Worth knowing about, seldom worth trading.
economicCalendar.impactHolidayBody: A market is closed. Thin liquidity can make an ordinary move look far larger than it is.
economicCalendar.actualBody: The figure as released. Price reacts to the distance between this and the forecast, not to the figure on its own.
economicCalendar.forecastBody: What economists expected. It is already priced in before the release lands.
economicCalendar.previousBody: Last period's reading, so you can see the direction of travel. It is sometimes revised on the day.
economicCalendar.timezoneTitle: Times are shown in your own timezone
economicCalendar.timezoneBody: The calendar detects your timezone and offers a clock control in its header to change it. Use the settings icon to filter by currency and by impact, and the date control to step between weeks and months.
economicCalendar.openLabel: Open the calendar in a new tab
economicCalendar.unavailableBody: The calendar is supplied by a third party and loads in a frame. If it stays blank, a browser extension or a network policy is the likely cause — open it in a new tab instead.
economicCalendar.attribution: Calendar data supplied by the MQL5 Economic Calendar.
economicCalendar.heroFootnote: Times, filters and event detail are supplied by the embedded calendar. Nothing here is a recommendation to trade.
economicCalendar.calendarLead: Step between weeks and months, filter by currency and by impact, and set your own timezone from the calendar's own controls.
economicCalendar.columnsLead: Three figures sit beside every release. The gap between the first two is what actually moves price.

economicCalendar.howToStepFour: Decide in advance whether you will hold, hedge, or stand aside through each one.

hero.title: Learn the markets with MBX
hero.body: The MBX Learning Center is where we explain how trading actually works — in plain language, with worked examples, and without pretending anything is risk-free.

offer.title: Ways in, depending on how you learn
offer.lead: Take the structured route from the beginning, or dip in wherever you already are.

courses.title: Structured courses
courses.body: Work through the fundamentals in order — what moves a currency pair, how an order fills, how to size a position.

glossary.title: Plain-language glossary
glossary.body: Every term you will meet, defined without jargon and cross-linked so one definition leads to the next.

analysis.title: Market analysis
analysis.body: What happened, why it mattered, and which levels traders were watching — written after the move, never sold as a prediction.

news.title: Market news
news.body: The headlines that actually change how a market trades, filtered from the ones that do not.

tools.title: Calculators and tools
tools.body: Position size, pip value, margin and profit — the arithmetic worked out so you can check your own.

calendar.title: Economic calendar
calendar.body: The releases that move markets, with dates and consensus, so nothing catches you mid-trade.

principles.title: How we teach
principles.lead: Four commitments that shape everything published here.
principles.plainLanguage: Plain language first. Every term is defined where it appears and linked to the glossary — we assume no vocabulary you have not been given.
principles.workedExamples: Worked examples over theory. Real numbers and real charts, with the arithmetic shown rather than asserted.
principles.riskIncluded: Risk is part of the lesson, never an appendix. What can go wrong is taught alongside what can go right.
principles.notAdvice: Education, not advice. Nothing here is a signal, a recommendation, or guidance about your own money.

founded.title: Ten lessons and a spreadsheet
founded.body: MBX starts as a set of evening classes for friends who kept asking the same questions about leverage. The first curriculum fits on one page.

curriculum.title: A curriculum, not a blog
curriculum.body: The lessons are rewritten in order, each one building on the last, with a worked example and a risk note attached to every concept.

glossary.title: The glossary opens
glossary.body: Every term used in a lesson gets its own definition, cross-linked both ways, so nobody has to leave a lesson to look something up.

languages.title: Reading right to left
languages.body: The platform is rebuilt around logical layout properties so an Arabic or Urdu reader gets the same design rather than a mirrored afterthought.

surge.title: A year of full rooms
surge.body: Enrolment triples. The support inbox tells us what the curriculum was missing, and beginner material is reorganised around what people actually ask first.

analysis.title: The analysis desk
analysis.body: Daily market notes begin — written after the move, explaining what happened and why, never predicting the next one.

mentors.title: Mentors, not signals
mentors.body: Learners get scheduled sessions with someone who reviews their trading journal. We turn down every offer to resell entry signals.

calendar.title: The economic calendar
calendar.body: Releases, forecasts and prior values land in one place, tied back to the lessons that explain what each number moves.

recognition.title: First recognition
recognition.body: The curriculum is named in its first industry listing, judged on how much of it is free to read without an account.

accessibility.title: Rebuilt for everyone
accessibility.body: A full accessibility pass: keyboard paths, contrast thresholds derived rather than hand-picked, and a dark mode the reader controls.

platform.title: One platform, four languages
platform.body: Courses, glossary, analysis and tools move onto a single codebase with translation built into the foundations instead of bolted on.

today.title: Where we are now
today.body: Tens of thousands of learners, a curriculum that still starts at the beginning, and the same rule as the first evening class: explain it or cut it.

hero.title: Why learn the markets here
hero.body: Anyone can publish a chart with an arrow on it. Here is what we do differently — and what we will never do.

commitments.title: What you can hold us to
commitments.lead: Five things that are true of everything published in the Learning Center.
commitments.noAccount: You can read everything here without an account and without funding anything.
commitments.noSignals: We never sell trading signals, tips, or strategies described as guaranteed.
commitments.afterTheMove: Analysis explains a move that has already happened. It is never dressed up as a forecast of the next one.
commitments.riskInline: Risk warnings sit with the content they apply to, not only in the footer.
commitments.ownProducts: Where a lesson refers to MBX products, it says so plainly instead of implying neutrality.

reasons.title: What makes this worth your time

curriculum.title: A curriculum, not a pile of content
curriculum.body: Lessons run in order and build on each other, so you always know what came before a topic and what it prepares you for. Start at the beginning or join where you already are.

glossary.title: Definitions you can actually use
glossary.body: Every term is written for someone meeting it for the first time, with an example rather than a circular restatement — and cross-linked, so one definition leads you to the next.

analysis.title: Analysis that explains rather than predicts
analysis.body: We write about what moved, why it moved, and which levels traders were watching while it did. That is a lesson you can reuse; a price target is not.

tools.title: The arithmetic done for you
tools.body: Position size, pip value, margin, profit and loss — worked out step by step so you can check the numbers yourself rather than take ours on trust.

support.title: A person on the other end
support.body: When a lesson does not land or a platform question gets in the way, you can reach someone. Support is part of the education, not a separate department.

cta.title: See it for yourself
cta.description: Read a lesson, look up a term, or check a calculation. Nothing here asks you to sign up first.

hero.title: How we operate
hero.body: Where the numbers on this site come from, how they reach you, and what we will and will not do with your attention.

sources.title: Where our numbers come from
sources.body: Market prices, rates and calculator inputs come from our market-data provider. Everything shown here is indicative and published for learning: it is not a dealing price, and it should not be used as one.

delivery.title: How it reaches you
delivery.lead: Four surfaces, one source. A number that changes changes everywhere.
delivery.web: The pages you are reading now, on any screen size.
delivery.articles: News and analysis, with the date and the author on every piece.
delivery.glossary: The glossary, cross-linked from every lesson that uses a term.
delivery.tools: The calculators, which show their working rather than just an answer.

funding.title: How the Learning Center is funded
funding.body: The Learning Center is published by MBX. It does not charge for access and it does not carry advertising. Where a lesson or an article refers to an MBX product, it says so rather than implying neutrality.

notDoing.title: What we don't do
notDoing.lead: Commitments about the content itself, not about the markets.
notDoing.noSignals: We do not sell signals, copy-trading, or managed accounts through the Learning Center.
notDoing.noTargets: We do not publish price targets, and we never describe an outcome as guaranteed.
notDoing.noSilentEdits: We do not quietly rewrite published analysis. A correction is marked as a correction.
notDoing.noPaidEditorial: We do not present a paid placement as editorial.

example.title: We show the arithmetic
example.body: A standard lot is 100,000 units of the base currency. One pip on EUR/USD is 0.0001, so one pip on a standard lot is $10 — and on 0.10 lots, $1. Every calculator here shows that working, so you can check it rather than trust it.
example.caption: 1 pip · EUR/USD · 0.10 lots

corrections.title: When we get it wrong
corrections.body: Mistakes are corrected in place, with a note saying what changed and when. Analysis is a record of what we thought at the time; editing that record silently would make it worthless.

hero.title: Security and trust
hero.body: How your account is protected, what happens to your data, and what gets written down when something changes.

account.title: How your account is protected
account.argon: Passwords are hashed with Argon2id. We never store one, log one, or email you one.
account.sessions: Sessions live in our database rather than only in a token, so a session can actually be revoked.
account.backoff: Repeated failed sign-ins slow down with an increasing delay instead of locking you out permanently.
account.cookies: Sign-in cookies are HTTP-only, so no script running on the page can read them.

data.title: What we do with it
data.minimal: We ask for what an account needs, and no more.
data.nonPublic: Settings marked non-public never reach a public page's data payload.
data.audit: Every administrative change is written to an audit log — who, what, and when.

platform.title: How the site itself is built
platform.body: The defences that matter are the ones a visitor never sees.
platform.sanitised: Anything an editor writes is sanitised on the server before it is stored, not merely inside the editor.
platform.uploads: Uploads are identified by their leading bytes, never by the filename or the type a browser claims.
platform.csp: The site sends a Content Security Policy, and the administration area gets a stricter one than the public pages.
platform.permissions: Every change is permission-checked on the server. A hidden button is not security, so we do not treat it as any.
